topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and context for the lecture on the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central C3 activation hub of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the alternative, lectin, and classical recognition pathways activate complement and reach a shared threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the downstream effector mechanisms triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the protective regulatory proteins and mechanisms host cells use to prevent self-damage from complement.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct clinical phenotypes and diseases that result from deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the diverse evolutionary strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on adaptive immunity.
